title: Free AI PDF reader: summarise a PDF or turn it into Excel · {name}
description: Drop a PDF in a browser tab and ask: a summary, the dates and amounts, its tables as an Excel workbook, a translation in Word. Free, nothing to install.
h1: Ask your PDF anything, or turn its tables into Excel.
lede: Drop a PDF in {name} and ask in your own words: what it commits you to, the dates and amounts it sets, a summary for someone who won’t read it. Its tables come back as a workbook, its text as a Word document, in your language if you like. Nothing to install.
cta.note: There is no sample PDF: bring one of yours, one that isn’t confidential to start with, and drop it in the box.
pane.ask: Put every transaction in an Excel workbook.
pane.answer: Here is your workbook: a row per transaction, the totals as formulas.
replay.title: One task, step by step.
replay.why: A bank statement as a PDF, made a workbook: what {name} read, what it worked out, and the files it made.
replay.ask: Put every transaction of this statement in an Excel workbook, one row each, with the money in and out added up. Check the totals against the statement’s.
replay.reads: The statement’s text, page by page
Its table of transactions, and its own totals
replay.works: Rebuilt each row: its date, its label, the money in or out
Added them up with a program, on the computer in its sandbox
Compared those totals with the statement’s
replay.got: A workbook: the transactions on one sheet, the totals on another, the sums as formulas.
replay.again: And a short note for my accountant, in Word, with anything unusual.
replay.made: A Word document with the month’s totals and what stood out, as a card under the answer, to change and send.

exact.title: Totals worked out, not guessed.
exact.why: Copying figures by hand is where mistakes creep in. {name} reads them from the PDF and has them added up.
exact.cards: Figures come from the PDF’s own text, as it was written, not from a picture of it.
Totals and averages are calculated on a computer in a sandbox, in this tab, never your own machine. The first time, {name} asks before turning it on.
Each step shows as it runs. Open one to see what it was given and what came back.
where.title: Where your PDF goes.
where.why: There is no {name} server. What changes is the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: Your files and your tasks are kept in this browser, encrypted. Nothing reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and the PDF’s text go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
With the AI on this computer, nothing leaves it: the one for a payslip or a medical letter. It needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. No sign-up only with the AI on this computer.
A scanned PDF, with no text in it, isn’t read. A photo of the page is, by an AI that sees pictures.
It doesn’t change a PDF or make one: it makes a Word document, which Word saves as PDF.
A PDF’s layout isn’t kept: in Word, you get its text, headings and tables, not its look.
A table read from a PDF is rebuilt from its text: check a few rows against the original.
{name} can be wrong. Numbers are calculated; check the words, as you would a colleague’s.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Can it read a scanned PDF?
Not as a PDF: a scan has no text in it to read. Take a photo or a screenshot of the page instead, for an AI that sees pictures.
How long can the PDF be?
Up to 100 MB. A long one is read a part at a time, the pages a question needs found by search.
Can it turn a PDF into Word?
It writes a Word document from the PDF’s text, with its headings, lists and tables. The layout isn’t copied.
It is kept on your device, encrypted. Its text goes to the AI you chose, to answer; with the AI on this computer, nowhere.
Yes: PDFs in Chinese, Japanese, Arabic and many more, and it answers in yours.
end.title: Start with a PDF that isn’t confidential.
end.why: {name} opens with its box ready. Drop the PDF in, and ask.
